items.heading: ### "Build fails with checksum mismatch error"
items.text: With this layout every `./judo.sh build` formats the generated frontend code after writing it (`pnpm run format`, Biome), so the generated files never match their checksums. Use `./judo.sh build -i` for every build; without `-i` each generated file of `src/` is reported as manually changed. `-i` leaves `.generated-files` of the frontend module empty, so the checksum protection cannot be turned on later without regenerating `src/`.
items.evidence: judo-ng target/judo-ng-read/wt/template__judo-ui-react-template/openspec/specs/integration-testing/spec.md:17 (generate-sources runs pnpm install and pnpm run format); app: webshop-test build without -i reported every file of src/ (build log), .generated-files 0 bytes after build -i

items.heading: #### In TransferObjectType (unmapped)
items.text: An actor reaches a static operation on an unmapped transfer object through a derived access on the actor whose target is a mapped transfer object: map a transfer object to a row of the model (for example a settings entity with no members), declare the STATIC operation on that transfer object, and add a DERIVED 0..1 access on the actor to that row (for example `<Entity>!any()`). The access target must be mapped; the row must exist at runtime, otherwise the access is empty. The REST route is `POST /api/<app>/<Actor>/<TransferObject>/<operation>` with the input as the JSON body; a fault returns 422 with `X-Fault`. A void static operation is possible.

items.heading: ### Practice notes: a fragment for `application_default.json`
items.text: The fragment is included at the top of the generated `application_default.json`. A key that the generator writes later in the same object (for example `enumerations.<Enum>.<MEMBER>`) overrides a duplicate key from the fragment, so an override of a generated key has no effect. An enumeration member has no label in the model, so a readable label needs a key that the generator does not write, or the model name is shown.
items.evidence: judo-ng target/judo-ng-read/wt/template__judo-ui-react-template/judo-ui-react/src/main/resources/actor/public/i18n/application_default.json.hbs:7 (fragment included first, generated keys after); app: webshop-test generator-overrides/ui-react/actor/public/i18n/application_default_extra.fragment.hbs (line not recorded).

items.heading: ## Cards Configuration Hook
items.text: The proxy of a custom relation element receives `ownerData`, `isOwnerLoading`, `actions` and `editMode`, but no refresh counter. A custom list learns about a page refresh only through a change of the identity of `ownerData`; the generated table gets a refresh counter, the proxy does not.
items.evidence: judo-ng target/judo-ng-read/wt/template__judo-ui-react-template/judo-ui-react/src/main/resources/actor/src/custom/interfaces.ts.hbs:23-30 (TableProxyProps has no refreshCounter); LazyTable.tsx.hbs:98 (table side has refresh handling).

items.heading: ## Cards Configuration Hook
items.text: The `ActionbarElement` of the cards hook is the only place for a cards container's create button, table operation buttons (for example an export), progress bar and empty state. The cards do not render these; a list without `ActionbarElement` shows none of them.

items.heading: ### Placement
items.text: In the horizontal top bar the navigation takes `8 - spaceRequired` of the 12 grid columns and the right side takes `2 + spaceRequired`; the default `spaceRequired` is 1. The scroll arrows of the menu reserve space too. A top bar with five or more menu groups plus search, switches, cart and profile needs a larger `spaceRequired` and a compact extra component (for example no wrapping, narrow profile name, icon-only search); at 1280px the last menu group can sit behind a scroll arrow.

items.heading: #### Creating, filling and changing elements
items.text: - **`MimeType`** has no `name` in its `CreateInput` either (the name derives from type and subType); `create -t MimeType -n ...` fails. Working form: `create -t MimeType --ns <ns> -s type=application -s subType=json` (creates `application/json`). `BinaryType.mimeTypes` takes one value on `create`: `-s mimeTypes=a,b` is rejected (`'b' is not an allowed value`), and the error lists the valid values as object hashes; the multi-value form was not found.
